title: Building Up Skin Models for Numerous Applications - from Two-Dimensional (2D) Monoculture to Three-Dimensional (3D) Multiculture
protocol: Perform skin cell culture in flasks dedicated for adherent or suspension cells.
Maintain cultures at 37°C and 5% carbon dioxide content in an incubator.
Prepare sterile conditions in a laminar chamber after exposing it to ultraviolet C (UVC) rays for 15-30 min.
Remove the medium from the culture flask.
Gently wash the cells with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add trypsin solution in ethylene diamine tetra acetic acid (trypsin-EDTA solution).
Incubate the flask at 37 °C and control the detachment of cells from the surface on the optical microscope.
Suspend the detached cells in at least a double amount of full-growth medium or trypsin neutralizer to deactivate trypsin (2:1).
Quantitatively transfer the content of the flask into the 15 mL tube.
Take a small volume (20 µL) of cell suspension into a 1.5 mL tube and count the cells with a manual or automatic hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the tube.
Remove most of the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the small amount of the remaining liquid.
Add enough fresh medium to obtain the pre-centrifugation volume if the cell density is appropriate to seed.
Remove the medium with the cell suspension from the culture flask and quantitatively transfer it into the 15 mL tube.
Take a small volume (20 μL) of the cell suspension into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Count the cells with a manual or automatic hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the tube according to parameters specified in Table 4.
Remove most of the supernatant and resuspend the cells in a small amount of the remaining liquid.
Add fresh medium to obtain the pre-centrifugation volume if the cell density is appropriate for seeding, otherwise recalculate the required volume of new medium.
Use trypsin neutralizator for keratinocytes and melanocytes during the detachment process.
Centrifuge detached cells at 300 x g, 5 min, RT after detaching them with trypsin.
Culture keratinocytes in Keratinocyte Growth Medium 2 supplemented with trypsin neutralizer.
Culture fibroblasts in DMEM containing 10% FBS without the need for trypsin neutralization.
Centrifuge mast cells at 300 x g, 3 min, RT after detaching them with trypsin.
Use an appropriate cell density to achieve the desired sphere size (recommended cell density 5 x 10^5 cells/mL).
Pipette 20 μL of the cell suspension on the lid of a Petri dish or multi-well plate.
Cover the dish/plate with the bottom part and gently flip it.
Fill the Petri dish/wells of the plate with a sterile water/PBS solution to avoid evaporation of the medium from droplets.
Incubate the droplets for 48-72 h at 37 °C.
Cover the wells of the U-bottom plate with a surfactant solution (e.g., Pluronic F-127, polyethylene glycol, polyvinyl alcohol).
Prepare and add 100 µL of 1% surfactant solution in PBS into each well.
Incubate the plate with the solution for 24 h at 37 °C.
Take 200 µL tips, remove 1/5 of each tip end, and sterilize before use.
Transfer the cell spheres to the wells of the multi-well plate by using sterile pipette tips with a cut end.
Prepare the cell suspension in a desired cell density of 2 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Seed 50 μL of the cell suspension per well in the plate.
Remove the surfactant solution from the wells before seeding to avoid cell membrane disruption by lysis.
Incubate the plate for 24 hours at 37 °C to allow cell aggregates to form.
After approximately 1-3 days, spheres will be formed and are ready for further experiments.
Place tubes with water, PBS (10x), 1 M NaOH, and type I collagen solution on ice.
Determine a proper number of dermal cells to be seeded in the hydrogel.
Transfer fibroblasts and mast cells to a 1.5 mL tube according to cell densities.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the cells.
Gently resuspend the cells in a mixture of 695 µL water, 100 µL PBS (10x), and 5 µL NaOH.
Add 200 µL of collagen solution to the cell mixture.
Gently mix the mixture by pipetting.
Add 200 µL of the prepared mixture to the insert in a 24-well plate.
For a model without stratum corneum, add 500 µL to each well of the 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 10 min at room temperature (RT).
Transfer the plate to an incubator for 30 min.
Check if the hydrogel has polymerized before proceeding with further actions.
Rinse the hydrogel with PBS buffer (500 µL/well) before cell seeding.
Determine the number of epidermal cells, such as keratinocytes and melanocytes (at a ratio of 15:1), to be seeded on top of the hydrogel.
Prepare the cell mixture in 500 µL of DMEM medium supplemented with 10% FBS by adding 250 µL of keratinocytes and 250 µL of melanocytes (cell densities are mentioned in Table 4).
Gently add the prepared cell mixture to the wells.
In some cases, first seed melanocytes and allow them to spread on the hydrogel for an additional 24 h before seeding keratinocytes.
If necessary, after seeding melanocytes, add 250 µL of cell suspension and 250 µL of medium.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 2-5 days depending on the speed of cell growth.
Exchange the medium every 48 h with a decreasing concentration of FBS from 10% to 1%.
Monitor cells on an optical microscope during incubation.
Induce keratinization after obtaining a monolayer of keratinocytes on top of the hydrogel.
Use FBS-free medium supplemented with calcium ions and L-ascorbic acid for induction.
Add calcium ions to the medium in a concentration of 1.5 µM CaCl2.
Add L-ascorbic acid to the medium at a concentration of 50 µg/mL.
Incubate the keratinocytes for an additional 2-7 weeks depending on their differentiation speed.
Wash the skin equivalent with PBS for 5 min at room temperature twice and fix it using a 3.7% paraformaldehyde solution in PBS (30 min, room temperature).
Repeat the washing step with PBS.
Incubate the skin equivalent in increasing concentrations of ethanol solutions: 50% (15 min), 70% (15 min), 96% (2x, 30 min each), and 99.8% (2x, 30 min each).
Put the fixed and dehydrated skin equivalent in the mold filled with paraffin.
Cover the mold with a cassette and add more paraffin on top.
Let it solidify for up to 30 min at room temperature.
Freeze the paraffin-embedded skin equivalent for at least 1 h at -80 °C.
Turn on the microtome, insert the paraffin-embedded skin equivalent, and cut 5 µm slices.
Place the cut artificial tissue slices on microscopic slides and dry them for at least 8 h at 37 °C.
Immerse the slides in xylene (2x, 10 min).
Rehydrate the slides with decreasing ethanol concentrations: 99.8% (5 min), 96% (5 min), 70% (5 min), and 50% (5 min).
Rinse the slides twice with water (5 min).
Stain the microscopic slide in hematoxylin solution for 3 min at room temperature.
Wash the slides in an acidified alcohol solution for 1 min.
Wash the slide in 0.1% sodium bicarbonate solution to obtain a visible, delicate blue-violet color.
Wash the slides with 95% ethanol for 1 min.
Stain the microscopic slide in eosin solution for 1 min at room temperature.
Wash the slides with 95% ethanol for 1 min.
Wash the slides with 99.8% ethanol for 2 min.
Wash the slides with xylene for 2 min each twice.
Mount in balsam and put a coverslip at the top of the slide.
Rinse the slide with PBS (phosphate-buffered saline) for 5 min.
Prepare the blocking solution (3% bovine serum albumin [BSA] or non-fat milk in PBS buffer with addition of 0.1% Triton X-100 and 0.1% Tween 20).
Incubate the slide in the blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the slides twice with a PBS buffer (5 min).
Dilute the primary antibody in the PBS buffer according to the producer's recommendations.
Incubate the slides for 1-2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the slides twice with a PBS buffer (5 min).
Dilute the secondary antibody in PBS buffer according to the producer's recommendations.
Incubate the slides with the diluted secondary antibody for 1 h at RT.
Wash the slides twice with PBS (5 min).
Prepare a dye solution for nuclei staining (e.g., Hoechst 33342 or DAPI) and incubate the slides for up to 15 min at RT.
Wash the slides with PBS (5 min).
Mount in balsam, cover the section with a coverslip, and visualize the effects of the cell staining using a fluorescent microscope.
Dilute the secondary antibody in a buffer appropriate for the conjugated enzyme according to the producer's recommendations.
Incubate the slides with the diluted secondary antibody for 1 h at RT.
Wash the slides twice with PBS (5 min).
Prepare a solution of a proper substrate for the used enzyme and incubate the slides according to the producer's recommendations.
Wash the slides with a buffer (5 min) and mount them in balsam.
Visualize the effects of the cell staining using bright-field microscopy.
